summary.text: St. Zosimas is the Palestinian monk and priest remembered for meeting St. Mary of Egypt, bringing her Communion and burying her.

blocks.text: The OCA identifies St. Zosimas as a monk in Palestine. The longer life of St. Mary of Egypt describes his move from a monastery near Caesarea to one by the Jordan after he becomes troubled by the thought that he has already attained spiritual maturity.

blocks.text: Following the monastery’s Lenten custom, he enters the wilderness and encounters St. Mary of Egypt. She tells him about her earlier life and repentance. As a priest he later brings her Holy Communion. When he returns again, he finds her dead and buries her. These events belong to the received life rather than a newly reconstructed eyewitness biography.

blocks.text: The OCA’s short entry says that St. Zosimas lived to a great age and died around 560. It does not give a martyrdom or execution account. Its received chronology should not be pressed into an exact modern birth date.

blocks.text: His commemoration is April 4. His identity is the Palestinian priest in St. Mary’s story, distinct from other monastics named Zosimas, including Russian Saints of later centuries.
